title: Irreversible Action Executed Without Confirmation
mitigation: Tag tools with `irreversible: true`. The dispatcher must require a confirmation_token whose hash equals SHA256(plan_id + tool_name + canonical(args)) and whose generation was logged in the prior turn. Without a matching token, the tool returns a 'pending confirmation' response instead of executing.
references: OWASP LLM08: Excessive Agency
Anthropic — Computer Use Safety Considerations

title: Private Session Data Sent to Non-Allowlisted External API
mitigation: Outbound HTTP from the agent goes through a single safePost wrapper that (1) checks the destination host against a fixed allowlist, (2) classifies the request body and rejects bodies containing private-tagged fields when the destination is not on an internal allowlist, (3) logs every outbound call with destination and content-class. Prefer per-tool destination allowlists (e.g., the Stripe tool can only POST to api.stripe.com) over a global one.
references: OWASP LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure
OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling
MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0024 — Exfiltration via API

title: Multi-Agent Delegation Expands Permission Scope
mitigation: Every delegation passes a capability token bound to the caller's permissions. The callee's dispatcher computes effective_permissions = caller_permissions ∩ callee_permissions for the delegated call. Tokens are short-lived, signed, and bound to a specific tool name. Without a valid token, the callee refuses the delegation.
references: OWASP LLM07: Insecure Plugin Design (delegation variant)
Capability-based security — confused deputy problem (Hardy 1988)

title: Cross-Agent State Channel Pollution
mitigation: Every shared-channel write records {writer_agent_id, session_id, signed_at, signature_over(value)}. Every read returns the value PLUS the provenance record. Consumers MUST verify the signature, MUST check that writer_agent_id is on the consumer's allowlist of trusted writers for that namespace, AND MUST scope the read to the session/tenant the consumer is currently serving. A shared channel without provenance is a stored-injection sink.
references: OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling (cross-context variant)
Stored XSS pattern — multi-agent generalization (Hardy/Madnick analogue, 2024)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-CHAIN-0001 (delegation-time confused deputy)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-RAG-0001 (single-agent context poisoning)

title: Untrusted Tool Output Evaluated as Code Downstream
mitigation: Tool outputs are typed data, not code. Downstream dispatch uses a fixed allowlist table indexed by an enum-typed action name. eval / Function / exec are forbidden in the agent runtime, enforced by a lint rule and CI gate. Tool outputs that cross trust boundaries are JSON-parsed in a structured shape and validated against a schema.
references: OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code
Semgrep — javascript.lang.security.audit.unsafe-eval

title: Cross-Tenant Memory Disclosure in Agent Long-Term Store
mitigation: Every memory read must include an owner-equality predicate against the authenticated principal. Owner is bound at write time from the verified session, not from caller-supplied input. Tenant isolation is a database-level invariant, not an LLM policy.
references: OWASP LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

title: System Instruction Disclosure via Output Reflection
mitigation: The output path passes through a strip layer that scans for known system-channel substrings (system prompt fingerprints, credential patterns, internal sentinel tokens) and refuses or redacts the response. Treat the system prompt as a secret; do not embed credentials in it; rotate fingerprint sentinels per deployment.
references: OWASP LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure
OWASP LLM01: Prompt Injection (extraction variant)

title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Long-Context Attention Drift
mitigation: Every retrieved document, tool output, or user-supplied content segment is wrapped with structural trust-boundary markers (e.g., <<<UNTRUSTED:doc_id>>>...<<<END_UNTRUSTED:doc_id>>>). The system prompt is re-emitted as an attention anchor after the untrusted block. A deterministic post-generation filter extracts imperatives from the model output and refuses any imperative whose semantic source traces to an untrusted region. Defense in depth: a final secret-scan output filter blocks known credential patterns regardless of source. Treat retrieved content as data, never as instructions.
references: OWASP LLM01: Prompt Injection (indirect/stored variant)
OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling
Greshake et al., 'Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection' (2023)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-PROMPT-0001 (direct system-prompt disclosure)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-RAG-0001 (retrieval-time context poisoning)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-CHAIN-0002 (multi-agent shared-channel pollution)

title: Untrusted Retrieved Content Crosses Trust Boundary
mitigation: Tag retrieved content with an explicit data-channel role and surround it with a sandbox boundary the model recognizes. Strip or escape control sequences in retrieved text. Never concatenate retrieved strings directly into the system prompt; use a structured message with role=tool or role=user with clear delimiters.
references: OWASP LLM01: Prompt Injection
OWASP LLM03: Training Data Poisoning (indirect via RAG corpus)
Greshake et al., Indirect Prompt Injection (2023)

title: RAG Context-Window Timing Side-Channel Exfiltration via Shared Prompt Cache
mitigation: Namespace every prompt/prefix/KV cache key by trust boundary (tenant or session id) so one tenant's warm entries can never be hit by another tenant's probe, AND equalize the observable response time to a fixed budget so cache hit/miss is indistinguishable from latency. Cache the answer for performance under a tenant-scoped key, but decouple observable timing from cache state. Add rate limiting + anomaly detection on prefix-extension probing patterns. Treat any cross-trust-boundary cache as a covert channel until proven timing-safe.
references: CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy
CWE-385: Covert Timing Channel
CWE-203: Observable Discrepancy
OWASP LLM02:2025 — Sensitive Information Disclosure
Gu et al., 'Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs' (2025) — timing side channels from shared prompt caching
'InputSnatch: Stealing Input in LLM Services via Timing Side-Channel Attacks' (2024)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-RAG-0001 (retrieval-time context poisoning)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-MEM-0001 (memory disclosure across isolation boundary)
Related canon entry: VC-AI-PROMPT-0002 (indirect prompt injection via long-context attention drift)

title: Session Secrets Leaked via Tool Call Arguments
mitigation: Secrets live in a server-side capability vault. Tools receive an opaque handle (capability:abc123) in their args. The dispatcher dereferences handles immediately before invoking the tool implementation; the dereferenced secret never crosses the trace/log boundary. Loggers redact handle dereferences. The LLM context never contains a raw secret; it sees only handles.
references: OWASP LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
Capability-based security (Dennis & Van Horn 1966)

title: Agent-Coerced SSRF to Internal and Metadata Endpoints
mitigation: Wrap every outbound fetch in a guard that resolves the host, rejects RFC1918, link-local (169.254.0.0/16), loopback (127.0.0.0/8), IPv6 ULA/loopback, and known cloud-metadata hostnames. Re-validate after each redirect. Prefer an allowlist of known external destinations over a blocklist. The agent's URL-fetch tool is the only path; no second tool may issue HTTP.
references: OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling (SSRF variant)
Capital One 2019 breach — IMDSv1 SSRF via WAF
OWASP API Top 10 — API7 SSRF

title: Privileged Tool Call Without Permission Gate
mitigation: Wrap every tool dispatch in a permission gate keyed by (session_id, tool_name). Privileged tools must declare required capabilities, and the dispatcher must throw PermissionDeniedError if the active session does not hold them. Audit-log every privileged call.
references: OWASP LLM07: Insecure Plugin Design
MITRE ATLAS: AML.T0053 — LLM Plugin Compromise
